title: Security review: region pinning, KMS escrow & exception flows - SummitForge
summary: Discussion focused on region pinning and allowed exceptions for cross-border processing, KMS custody and escrow options, subprocessor disclosures, SOC 2 and audit log retention, and next steps to run a short pilot with VPC + KMS binding. Customer requested a written exception workflow and SOC 2 plus ISO artifacts.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-02-14 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Avery, Marcus, Priya (Redwood) — Elena, Tomislav, Rosa, Kai, Nadia (SummitForge)

[00:00] Avery Holt: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. quick intro - i'm avery, i'm the account lead, with me is marcus from solutions engineering and priya from customer success. how about we do quick intros on the summitforge side?

[00:12] Elena Marquez: sure, elena here - head of it at summitforge, we manage a bunch of clinical ingestion pipelines and patient-facing ui, so residency is a big one for us.

[00:23] Tomislav Ilic: tomislav, security architect - i'll be focused on key management, audit, and the exception process for cross-border tasks.

[00:30] Rosa Park: rosa - legal counsel; DPA, subprocessors, and change control for our contracts.

[00:38] Avery Holt: great. quick agenda: region pinning model, exceptions for cross-border, KMS options incl escrow, subprocessors inventory and notification cadence, SOC2/ISO artifacts, and then next steps. any other items?

[00:49] Kai Nakamura: one ask — can we get details on audit log retention and SIEM hooks?

[00:55] Marcus Chen: yes for sure. we'll cover logs and RBAC mapping.

[01:05] ----- Topic: region pinning -----

[01:10] Marcus Chen: at a high level, our region pinning means you can declare a processing affinity per route or per model. requests with tagged eu personal data will be routed to eu-hosted pools — that only serve that tenant's workloads. we call it region affinity not strict lock sometimes because there are exception paths.

[01:35] Tomislav Ilic: right, that 'exception path' is what concerns us. if we have a spike and the eu pool is saturated, what's the formal process for an exception to send to us-east? we can't have egress of raw PII without legal approval.

[01:50] Avery Holt: valid. we support strictly enforced pinning — you can set a hard region lock. when you do that, automatic fallback is disabled. for customers that want flexible failover, we have an exception workflow: the request can be routed to an alternative region if you enable cross-border exceptions, but it leaves an auditable trail and requires pre-approved rules.

[02:12] Elena Marquez: auditable trail — meaning an alert and a human signoff?

[02:17] Marcus Chen: it's both. we emit a structured event into the audit log with the request id, model, input hash, and reason code. you get a high-severity alert in the console and we can also push webhook notifications to an on‑prem endpoint. the event includes whether KMS was applied and which key domain was used.

[02:37] Nadia Ortiz: is that webhook payload stable? we want to sink into our siem.

[02:41] Marcus Chen: yes, but note sometimes the field names in the webhook changed across runtime versions — apologies, the client library v1.3 rename happened last quarter so some fields could be slightly different in older integrations.

[02:58] ----- Topic: KMS custody & escrow -----

[03:05] Tomislav Ilic: let's talk KMS. we require EU keys for EU resident data. what's the support for bring-your-own-key (BYOK) and can you do HSM-backed keys under our control?

[03:16] Marcus Chen: we support three patterns: 1) Redwood-managed keys — easiest, keys stored in Redwood's KMS and used by our runtime; 2) BYOK via cloud KMS integrations (you provide key in GCP KMS / AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault) and we never persist the key material — we integrate via IAM roles; 3) HSM/escrow: for customers who need offline custody we offer a KMS escrow option with a third party escrow vendor where key material can be split-shared.

[03:45] Rosa Park: escrow — so the key never leaves our custody unless we ask the escrow provider? i want the exact legal wording.

[03:52] Avery Holt: the escrow arrangement means the key is under a split‑control arrangement. Redwood can operate with a wrapped key and only with a quorum of parties can the unwrapped material be reconstructed. we'll provide the escrow MSA addendum and the escrow vendor list. we'll also show the operational runbook for key rotation and compromise scenarios.

[04:12] Tomislav Ilic: what's the latency impact if we use BYOK vs Redwood-managed?

[04:18] Marcus Chen: negligible for most workloads. BYOK integrations use ephemeral wrapping so per-token latency adds on the order of single-digit milliseconds for the unwrap on the first call; subsequent tokens use KV cache. HSM-backed unwrap can add a bit more if each operation queries the HSM, so we recommend local wrapping/fast cache.

[04:40] Kai Nakamura: can we co-locate the KMS in our eu region and have keys region-bound?

[04:44] Marcus Chen: yes, BYOK will let you bind keys to a region. the runtime will honor the key domain, and if region pinning is enabled, the request will failover-disabled unless you enable exceptions.

[04:59] ----- Topic: subprocessors and notification cadence -----

[05:05] Rosa Park: we need a list of subprocessors specific to EU regions and any changes to that list require 30 days notice and a materiality review. can you confirm your cadence?

[05:16] Avery Holt: we publish a subprocessors registry; for EU we show regional data centers, cloud partners, and any third-party monitoring or escrow vendors. our standard is 30 days notice for material subprocessor changes, and we can add stricter contract terms for enterprise agreements.

[05:31] Rosa Park: do you have local support partners who might get access during onboarding?"

[05:36] Priya Rao: yes, for private deployments we sometimes have an on-site engineering lead for first week of onboarding — access is time-limited, logged, and requires prior approval. we can scope that access out of the dpa.

[05:50] ----- Topic: audit logs, retention, SIEM integration -----

[05:55] Kai Nakamura: quick details: what fields are in the audit log? we need request id, user id, tenant id, model name, region, key-id, action type, decision reason, and evidence of consent if applicable.

[06:08] Marcus Chen: yes we emit all those. retention by default is 90 days on-hosted, 365 days for dedicated, and custom for private. for enterprise we can ship logs to your S3 or to a SIEM via syslog/webhook.

[06:21] Tomislav Ilic: any PII in logs? we must avoid storing raw inputs in centralized logs for eu personal data.

[06:28] Marcus Chen: by default, we hash inputs and store input-hash and metadata. you can opt for input redaction or zeroing — in private deployments the default is to not store raw inputs. we'll mark fields in the audit event that are redacted.

[06:45] ----- Topic: compliance artifacts & SLA -----

[06:50] Rosa Park: we need SOC 2 type II, ISO 27001 cert, encryption at rest docs, DPA, and an updated subprocessors list. also the SLA for latency when region pinned (what guarantees?)

[07:03] Avery Holt: we'll push our SOC 2 attestation and ISO cert. SLA depends on deployment: hosted has a 99.9% uptime commitment and best-effort latency, Dedicated has SLOs per customer contract. for region pinned routes we can commit to regional availability targets under Dedicated or Private options — we'll outline those in the pilot proposal.

[07:24] Nadia Ortiz: what about legal hold / e-discovery? if regulator asks for records, can we provide logs tied to a request?

[07:31] Priya Rao: yes, we have export tools and preserve modes for audit, with time-bound retention and chain of custody metadata. we'll detail the export format (parquet + manifest) in the artifacts.

[07:45] ----- Topic: exception workflow specifics -----

[07:50] Tomislav Ilic: walk me through a concrete exception flow: eu pool saturated at 03:00 CET, would you automatically route to us-east? what's the step-by-step for our reviewers?

[07:59] Marcus Chen: step 1: request hits runtime, region-match fails for available capacity; step 2: if strict-lock is on, request is rejected with a 403 and error code REGION_LOCKED; step 3: if cross-border exceptions are enabled and a rule exists, runtime creates a pending exception event with severity and pushes to your webhook; step 4: automated policy can allow limited low-sensitivity payloads via a transformed path (PII redaction) or the event must be approved by an admin via the console. once approved, the request is routed and the audit event persisted.

[08:32] Elena Marquez: is the admin approval synchronous? we need sub-5s user experience for some endpoints.

[08:37] Marcus Chen: admin approval is asynchronous — that would add latency. for low-latency needs we recommend pre-approved exception rules scoped by data class and rate-limits so the decision is automatic. that way no manual approval on the hotpath.

[08:53] Tomislav Ilic: and those pre-approved rules are visible in the audit log?

[08:57] Marcus Chen: yes each allowed rule has an id and you see which rule matched in the event.

[09:04] ----- Natural speech / misc noise and clarifications -----

[09:06] Rosa Park: quick legal Q — can we get a sample clause for the DPA addendum around escrow and split keys?

[09:12] Avery Holt: yes we'll attach a redline-ready clause.

[09:16] Elena Marquez: also, do you support per-tenant RBAC mapping with our SAML provider?

[09:20] Marcus Chen: yes SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning and role mapping. we map idp groups to internal roles and can sync every 24 hours or via SCIM push. some older customer integrations have had group name mismatch issues — sorry about that, it's usually config drift.

[09:39] ----- Vendor & competitor callouts -----

[09:41] Tomislav Ilic: competitors like bigcloudai claim they have more granular region control — how is redwood different?

[09:47] Avery Holt: Redwood emphasizes production controls and auditable exception flows with KMS binding. we also provide more explicit escape hatches like escrow and hardened private deployments.

[09:58] ----- Recap and next steps -----

[10:01] Avery Holt: recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, KMS escrow whitepaper, subprocessors registry, and a pilot runbook for BYOK+VPC. you'll share EU workload list. actions and owners are in the notes.

[10:15] Rosa Park: please include timeline for contract addenda for escrow and the 30-day subprocessor notice in the draft.

[10:22] Marcus Chen: we'll include an appendix that shows performance delta for BYOK vs managed keys using a representative 512-token workload.

[10:30] Elena Marquez: thanks, this was helpful. familiar note — we will want a short security deep dive with our infra team during pilot.

[10:36] Avery Holt: absolutely, we'll schedule a 60-minute technical kickoff — targeting the week of feb 28.

[10:42] Meeting end: 16:52 UTC
